title: Determination of the Transport Rate of Xenobiotics and Nanomaterials Across the Placenta using the ex vivo Human Placental Perfusion Model
protocol: Set up the perfusion system with a water bath, two peristaltic pumps, and other necessary components.
Connect the components using silicone and polyvinyl chloride tubing according to the specified scheme.
Turn on the water bath and set the temperature to 37 °C.
Warm up the perfusion medium in the water bath.
Rinse the arterial systems of the fetal and maternal circuits with distilled water.
Rinse the arterial systems with 1% sodium hydroxide.
Rinse the arterial systems with 1% phosphoric acid.
Rinse the arterial systems again with distilled water.
Connect the fetal cannula to the fetal arterial tubing.
Rinse arterial systems of the fetal and maternal circuit with perfusion medium until tubes contain medium (flow rate: 15-20 ml/min).
Fill up bubble traps and remove bubbles downstream of the trap.
Stop the pumps to ensure afferent arterial tubes are free of bubbles.
Turn on gas flow for maternal circuit with 5% carbon dioxide and 95% synthetic air.
Oxygenate fetal circuit with 5% carbon dioxide and 95% nitrogen.
Start recording pressure sensor data.
Obtain intact placentae from uncomplicated term pregnancies after primary cesarean section.
Ensure written consent is given by the mothers before delivery.
Assure a healthy and intact placenta through visual inspection by midwives.
Cannulate the placenta carefully to avoid disruption in tissue.
Select an intact cotyledon at the marginal zone of the placenta without visible disruptions on the maternal side.
Tie up both associated branches of the umbilical artery and vein upstream to the later cannulation side by using surgical suture material, making two knots.
Make a suture around the fetal artery but do not tie it immediately.
Hold the vessel with forceps, cut the vessel carefully, and put the small cannula (Ø 1.2 mm) into the artery.
Tie up the suture around the fetal artery with two knots.
Proceed to cannulate the fetal vein in the same manner using a bigger cannula (Ø 1.5-1.8 mm) attached to a modified winged needle infusion set with a blunt needle.
Turn on the fetal pump at 2 ml/min.
Increase the flow up to 4 ml/min if there is no visible leak and blood emanates out of the fetal vein cannula.
Fix any leaking fluid from the fetal or maternal cannulas with another suture.
Place the placenta on the tissue holder with the fetal side up.
Pull the placental membrane and tissue over the spikes, ensuring that the perfused cotyledon is in the middle of the hole in the tissue holder.
Stabilize the part where only the membrane holds the placenta with a silicone membrane (Ø 1 mm) or two parafilm pieces.
Assemble the complete tissue holder.
Tighten the screws.
Cut the overhanging tissue.
Turn the tissue holder upside down.
Place it into the perfusion chamber and add the cover.
Check that the fetal circuit remains intact and medium flows out of the fetal vein tubing.
Turn on the maternal pump (12 ml/min).
Introduce three blunt cannulae (Ø 0.8 mm) at the end of the maternal artery tube into the intervillous space by penetrating the decidual plate.
Connect one tube as venous drain to return perfusate to the maternal circuit and place it in the lowest position in the upper part of the perfusion chamber.
Connect the fetal vein cannula to the fetal vein tube.
Allow a 20-minute open pre-phase for tissue recovery from ischemia and flushing out blood from the intervillous space.
Perform a pre-phase of 20 minutes in a closed circuit to assess perfusion integrity.
Use two separate reservoirs with perfusion medium, one for the fetal circuit and one for the maternal circuit.
Close the fetal circuit by leading the venous outflow back into the fetal reservoir.
Close the maternal circuit by leading the venous outflow back into the maternal reservoir.
Prepare two flasks containing 120 ml of perfusion medium (one for each circuit).
Add radiolabeled 14C-antipyrine to the maternal reservoir at a concentration of 4 nCi/ml.
Add fluorescently labeled xenobiotic or nanoparticles to the maternal reservoir for analysis.
Mix the maternal perfusate thoroughly before starting the experiment.
Exchange pure perfusion medium with the prepared flasks (one for each circuit) to begin the main experiment.
Continue perfusion for 6 hours, taking regular samples throughout.
Resuspend the medium in both the fetal and maternal reservoirs immediately before withdrawing samples.
Control the pressure in the fetal artery to not exceed 70 mmHg.
Maintain pH in both circuits within a physiological range of 7.2-7.4.
Monitor volume loss in the fetal reservoir, ensuring it does not exceed 4 ml/hr.
Adjust pH values using hydrochloric acid or sodium hydroxide if necessary.
Stop perfusion immediately if there is a leak detected in the tissue.
End the perfusion after 6 hours.
Turn off the pumps, water bath, flow heaters, and gas flow.
Remove the placenta from the tissue holder.
Cut out the perfused cotyledon, which appears brighter than unperfused tissue.
Weigh the cut-out cotyledon.
Take samples of approximately 1 g each from unperfused and perfused tissues.
Store unperfused tissue samples at -20 °C for later homogenization or in liquid nitrogen for analysis.
Store perfused tissue samples at -20 °C for later homogenization or in liquid nitrogen for analysis.
Fix a separate tissue sample in 4% formalin for histopathological evaluation.
Include all layers of the placenta in the fixed tissue sample for analysis.
Rinse the arterial systems of both fetal and maternal circuits with 200 ml distilled water at a flow rate of 15-20 ml/min.
Rinse with 50 ml 1% sodium hydroxide solution at a flow rate of 15-20 ml/min.
Rinse with 50 ml 1% phosphoric acid solution at a flow rate of 15-20 ml/min.
Finally, rinse the arterial systems again with 200 ml distilled water at a flow rate of 15-20 ml/min.
Centrifuge the perfusate samples for 10 min at 800 x g before analysis.
Take the supernatant for further analysis.
Store the samples overnight at 4 °C if needed.
Mix 300 μl of fetal and maternal samples with 3 ml scintillation cocktail.
Measure the mixture for 5 min in a beta counter to analyze 14C-antipyrine.
Read the fluorescence at 485 nm excitation and 528 nm emission for nanoparticle analysis.
Measure glucose consumption and lactate production in fetal and maternal circuits using an automated blood gas system.
Evaluate the viability of placental tissue during perfusion based on metabolic parameters.
